name: wazero
recipe: No buildable recipe via lanes A-D. wazero is a pure-Go library/CLI; the only in-sandbox path is `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build` on its interpreter backend (which is platform-agnostic pure Go, no cgo/JIT — wasm-in-wasm is physically sound for the INTERPRETER mode only; the optimizing-compiler/AOT backend does native codegen and is impossible). But that path requires a Go->wasm toolchain, which is NOT one of our lanes (A=prebuilt, B=C/C++, C=Rust/mrustc, D=Python/JS) and not in the LIVE set. We have no in-sandbox Go compiler.
smoke: N/A — nothing to build. If a Go->wasm lane existed: GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build ./cmd/wazero with build tag forcing interpreter, then `wazero.wasm run hello.wasm` under wasmtime and assert stdout. Not achievable today.
blocker: Go source only — no prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact published (releases ship Go source + native CLI binaries). Building it needs a Go->wasm (GOOS=wasip1) toolchain, which is outside lanes A-D and absent from the in-sandbox toolchain set. Lane B/C/D inapplicable (pure Go, not C/Rust/Python/JS). Only the interpreter backend would be runtime-legal; the AOT compiler backend does native codegen (JIT) = forbidden.

name: GHC RTS (Haskell)
recipe: The GHC RTS itself is not a standalone wasm artifact you fetch or build via the C/C++/Rust/Python/JS lanes — it is the Haskell runtime embedded into every program GHC's wasm backend emits. Runtime-soundness IS confirmed: a plain Haskell executable (no JSFFI) compiles to a wasm32-wasi COMMAND module and runs directly under wasmtime ("wasmtime run foo.wasm --bar +RTS --nonmoving-gc -RTS"), pure AOT via STG — no JIT, no JS host, no fork-exec, no native threads required (single-threaded RTS by default; nonmoving GC available). WASI is the only syscall layer. JSFFI/reactor-module mode is opt-in and only for browser/JS interop, NOT required. BUT none of our 4 lanes apply: (A) no prebuilt plain .wasm exists for an arbitrary Haskell program — you must compile your own; (B/C/D) it is not buildable as a self-contained C/C++ tarball, a mrustc Rust crate, or pip/JS. Provisioning it requires adding the entire GHC wasm cross-compiler toolchain (wasm32-wasi-ghc from ghc-wasm-meta, a multi-hundred-MB nightly bindist for x86_64/aarch64-linux/darwin hosts) as a NEW compiler lane — a separate, large toolchain-integration effort, not a single-package import. Smoke would be: install ghc-wasm-meta, `wasm32-wasi-cabal build` a hello-world, `wasmtime run $(cabal list-bin exe:hello).wasm`.
smoke: wasm32-wasi-ghc -o hello.wasm Hello.hs && wasmtime run hello.wasm  # prints "Hello, World!" — proves STG RTS + GC + WASI runtime fully in-sandbox under wasmtime, no JS host
blocker: Runtime is sandbox-sound (wasm32-wasi command module under wasmtime, AOT STG, no JIT/JS/threads/fork). But it fits NONE of lanes A-D: no prebuilt arbitrary-program .wasm to fetch, and it cannot be built via C/C++/Rust/Python/JS lanes. Shipping Haskell support means integrating the full GHC wasm cross-compiler toolchain (ghc-wasm-meta, hundreds of MB) as a new compiler lane — a large standalone effort, not a package import.

name: R (R interpreter)
recipe: No viable recipe. R cannot be built as standalone wasm32-wasi under our C/C++/Rust toolchain. (1) Lane A: no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists. The only maintained wasm build is webR (r-wasm/webr), which is an Emscripten/JS-pair browser+Node build, not clean wasip1 — explicitly excluded. (2) Lane B (self-contained C/C++) fails: R's core is NOT pure C/C++. It links BLAS and LAPACK, which are Fortran, and many base routines are Fortran. webR had to extend its toolchain with a custom LLVM Fortran (flang-new/LFortran) cross-compiler just to produce liblapack.a/libblas.a for wasm — we have no Fortran compiler in the sandbox (only clang C/C++ and mrustc Rust). (3) R also requires a full autoconf configure that probes a Fortran compiler, readline, and platform features, plus Emscripten-specific source patches for its REPL/event loop — not pregeneratable into :include_only/:compile_only. (4) Not Rust (Lane C) and not Python/JS (Lane D).
smoke: N/A — cannot build. Hypothetical smoke would be: echo 'cat(1+1, "\n")' | r-wasm --no-save  expecting "2", but no buildable artifact exists.
blocker: R core depends on Fortran (BLAS/LAPACK + base Fortran routines); no Fortran compiler exists in the sandbox (only C/C++/Rust). The only wasm build (webR) is Emscripten/JS-pair, not wasip1, and requires a custom LLVM-Fortran toolchain plus autoconf-configure and Emscripten event-loop patches. None of lanes A-D can satisfy this.

name: RocksDB
smoke: N/A — no buildable wasip1 target. If one tried: rocksdb::DB::Open then Put/Get a key under wasmtime wasip1 — it would fail at Env background thread-pool init (pthread_create), since flush/compaction threads spawn at DB open before any write completes.
blocker: RocksDB is architecturally a multi-threaded background-compaction LSM engine: flush runs on a HIGH thread pool and compaction on a LOW thread pool (max_background_jobs), with real OS pthread spawning in its Env at DB open. This is foundational, not a perf knob — you cannot configure it down to a single in-thread loop (max_background_flushes=0 path was removed). wasip1 has no pthread spawn (single-thread). wasm32-wasip1-threads exists but requires shared memory + wasi-threads, which Wasmtime documents as experimental and explicitly NOT suitable for multi-tenant embeddings — exactly our isolated-instance sandbox model. RocksDB also leans on fsync durability semantics, jemalloc, and SIMD that fight wasip1. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists and no known port (only generic emscripten/browser experiments, none of RocksDB). The single-threaded embeddable KV niche is already covered by sqlite3 (LIVE).

name: LMDB
smoke: N/A — cannot build. Conceptual smoke if it did: mdb_env_open a file, mdb_put k/v, mdb_get reads it back, mdb_cursor scan. But LMDB cannot reach mdb_env_open under WASI: mdb_env_open mmaps the data file (MDB_WRITEMAP writes through the map) and uses fcntl/flock-style locks on a lockfile for MVCC reader/writer coordination — wasm32-wasi provides neither real mmap (only readonly emulation) nor file locking, so env setup fails.
blocker: LMDB's whole design = mmap() of a single data file (data IS the memory map; MDB_WRITEMAP writes through it) + file locks on a lockfile for MVCC reader/writer coordination. wasm32-wasi under wasmtime has no real mmap (WASI mmap is unimplemented/readonly-emulated only) and no file locking (flock/fcntl absent in wasi-libc). Confirmed by heed (Rust LMDB wrapper) maintainers: LMDB "won't compile to WASM/WASI because of its complicated concurrency model and reliance on other libc features... highly unlikely to compile for web for many years." Making it work would require reimplementing the storage backend on plain read/write/malloc — that is no longer LMDB. Not a Lane-B build/config problem; a missing-primitive problem. Note: sqlite3 is already LIVE and covers the embedded KV/transactional-store need without mmap dependence.

name: etcd
recipe: No viable lane. etcd is pure Go; the only live Go lane is yaegi (interpreter), which cannot run etcd's reflection/cgo-free-but-huge multi-package server tree, and Go-to-wasip1 native compilation is NOT a live lane here (we have no Go->wasm32-wasi toolchain in the compiler stack — lanes are A prebuilt .wasm, B C/C++, C bare Rust via mrustc, D pure-Python/JS-on-QuickJS). Even if Go compiled, etcd's entire purpose is the gRPC server + multi-node Raft consensus over real TCP sockets, which is network-as-purpose and forbidden in-sandbox.
smoke: N/A — cannot build. The storage/KV core (bbolt) would in principle build to wasip1, but no Go wasi lane exists and the product value (gRPC/Raft over TCP) is network-as-purpose. Hypothetical smoke would be a single-node embedded etcd Put/Get, but that is not what etcd is.
blocker: Network-as-purpose (gRPC server + multi-node Raft consensus over real TCP) is the entire value; additionally no Go->wasm32-wasi lane exists (only yaegi interpreter, insufficient for etcd's package tree).

name: InfluxDB
recipe: None viable. InfluxDB is a network-server database daemon, disqualified on multiple host-forbidden axes regardless of lineage. (1) InfluxDB 3.x (current, IOx): Rust on Apache Arrow/DataFusion/Parquet/Arrow-Flight. Its whole purpose is to listen on TCP and serve HTTP plus Arrow Flight gRPC queries = network-as-purpose. Runtime is tokio async network I/O plus rayon/DataFusion native thread pools for parallel query execution = native-threads. Huge Rust workspace, edition 2021/2024, heavy proc-macros (serde, tonic, async-trait) = Lane C mrustc ~1.74 impossible. (2) InfluxDB 1.x/2.x: Go. While Go has wasip1 in principle, InfluxDB is a goroutine-scheduled HTTP server daemon (net/http listener IS the product), needs real sockets plus filesystem-backed TSM storage engine plus background compaction goroutines. wasip1 has no sockets. Not Lane A/B/D either. The DataFusion columnar engine alone has wasm experiments, but that is a separate library, NOT InfluxDB-the-database.
smoke: N/A — no buildable/runnable single-binary in-sandbox artifact. If forced: influxd (1.x Go) or influxdb3 serve (3.x Rust) both immediately bind a TCP listener (default 8086 / 8181) and spawn a tokio/goroutine network reactor — fails the moment it calls socket()/listen() under wasmtime (no network), before any query smoke is possible.
blocker: network-as-purpose: InfluxDB is a server daemon whose reason to exist is listening on a TCP socket (HTTP + Arrow Flight/gRPC). Compounded by native-threads (tokio reactor + rayon/DataFusion thread pools) and, for 3.x, a huge edition-2021+ proc-macro Rust workspace mrustc cannot build. wasmtime gives no sockets and no native threads. sqlite3 already covers embedded SQL; InfluxDB has no embeddable single-threaded no-network mode.

name: Dgraph
recipe: No viable recipe. Dgraph is pure Go (~hundreds of kLOC), distributed across two binaries (Alpha storage nodes + Zero supervisor). None of the four lanes apply: not a prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact (A), not C/C++ (B), not a Rust crate buildable by mrustc (C), not pure-Python/JS (D). Go-to-wasip1 is technically a target but is not one of the offered lanes AND would not preserve Dgraph's value.
smoke: N/A — cannot reach a smoke test. The only meaningful smoke (run an Alpha+Zero cluster and POST a GraphQL/DQL mutation+query over gRPC/HTTP) requires network listeners and a multi-process cluster, both of which are the disqualifying capabilities.
blocker: Network-as-purpose: Dgraph's entire reason for existing is the distributed Alpha/Zero cluster that exposes gRPC + GraphQL/DQL servers over the network. Alpha uses Raft per-shard replication and gRPC; Zero forms a Raft cluster for membership/timestamp assignment. wasm32-wasi under wasmtime has no TCP listeners, no native OS threads for Raft/gRPC goroutine scheduling, and no fork-exec for the multi-binary cluster supervision. Stripping all that to just embed Badger as a local KV store is no longer Dgraph (it would be the badger lib, a different item, and badger is Go too). Confirmed pure-Go distributed-server architecture (Alpha=gRPC storage, Zero=Raft supervisor). Disqualified on network/native-threads grounds.

name: Firebird
recipe: No viable lane. No prebuilt wasm. C++ engine needs autoconf configure plus GPRE codegen, hard ICU data dep, and POSIX fcntl file locking plus shared-memory IPC. Not Rust, not Python/JS.
smoke: N/A. Would-be: isql embedded CREATE DATABASE then CREATE TABLE INSERT SELECT under wasmtime. Unreachable.
blocker: Embedded engine relies on POSIX fcntl file locking and shared-memory IPC, unavailable in wasm32-wasi; plus ICU data dep and configure+GPRE codegen build. SQLite already LIVE covers single-file embedded SQL.

name: KeyDB
recipe: N/A — out of scope for in-sandbox wasm32-wasi. KeyDB is a multithreaded C/C++ Redis fork whose defining feature is running the Redis event loop across native pthreads (network IO + query parsing concurrently, per-connection thread on accept). wasip1 has no pthreads/native threads without wasm-threads+shared-memory (unsupported under standalone wasmtime wasip1 here). Beyond threading, KeyDB's purpose is a network server (BSD sockets, epoll/kqueue event loop) and it uses fork() for RDB/BGSAVE persistence — fork-exec/network-as-purpose are explicitly disqualifying. No plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (only fringe single-threaded Redis-proper WASI experiments, not KeyDB, and those drop the server/network/fork model). Cannot build self-contained: it needs threads+sockets+fork that the sandbox forbids.
smoke: N/A — cannot run. If a single-threaded build somehow linked, `keydb-server` immediately needs to bind() a listening socket (network-as-purpose) and spawn worker threads, both unavailable; there is no meaningful offline/no-network smoke for a Redis server.
blocker: Native pthreads are the product's whole point (wasip1 has no threads); compounded by network-server-as-purpose (BSD sockets/epoll) and fork() for persistence. Threads+fork-exec+network all individually disqualifying under standalone wasmtime wasip1.

name: MonetDB
recipe: No viable recipe. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (only emscripten/browser experiments at best; nothing standalone). Lane B (self-build C via clang lane) is the only conceivable path but fails on architecture: MonetDB is a client-server system — mserver5 engine + monetdbd daemon — relying on fork-exec, the MAL interpreter runtime, mmap-backed (MAP_SHARED, writeback) column storage, pthreads-based parallel query execution, and POSIX advisory file locking. wasip1 provides none of these (no mmap writeback, no thread spawn, no fork-exec, no fcntl locking). Lane C/D N/A (not Rust/Python/JS). Even DuckDB — a far more self-contained single-process column store — only runs in wasm single-threaded with degraded out-of-core; MonetDB is strictly harder.
smoke: N/A — cannot build. If hypothetically built, smoke would be: pipe `SELECT 1;` to mserver5 in --dbpath over a single in-memory db and read scalar 1. Unreachable: mserver5 requires daemon fork, mmap dbfarm, and threads at startup.
blocker: Hard-depends on capabilities wasip1 lacks: fork-exec (monetdbd daemon + mserver5 process model), mmap MAP_SHARED writeback (column storage / BAT memory mapping), native pthreads (parallel MAL execution), and POSIX advisory file locking (dbfarm lock). None are emulatable in standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. Note: for analytics column-store coverage, sqlite3 is already LIVE; DuckDB would be the closer self-contained candidate, not MonetDB.

name: Qdrant
recipe: No viable recipe. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists; Qdrant ships only native server binaries / Docker images, not a standalone wasm module. Lane B: N/A (Rust, not C/C++). Lane C (mrustc ~1.74) is the only candidate lane and is impossible — the workspace is edition=2024, MSRV Rust 1.94, 15+ member crates (segment/collection/storage/shard/gridstore/wal/sparse/bm25/macros...), uses proc-macro crates (lib/macros + derive deps), tokio "full" and rayon. mrustc tops out well below edition 2024 and cannot handle real proc-macros or a workspace of this scale. Lane D: N/A. Even setting toolchain aside, the engine is a tokio gRPC/REST server whose purpose IS the network, with rayon native threads, mmap segments, and SIMD — all wasm32-wasi-hostile.
smoke: N/A — cannot produce a .wasm. If forced: `rustc --target wasm32-wasi` on lib/segment would fail at dependency resolution (tokio/rayon/mmap), and mrustc would reject edition-2024 + proc-macro crates before emitting anything.
blocker: edition=2024 + MSRV 1.94 + proc-macros + 15-crate workspace defeats mrustc ~1.74 (lane C, the only candidate). Core also requires native threads (rayon/tokio), mmap, SIMD, and is a gRPC/REST server (network-as-purpose) — all forbidden under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact exists.

name: Chroma
recipe: No viable lane. Chroma's core is a large multi-crate Rust workspace (~69% Rust, Cargo edition 2021+) built on tokio async runtime, native multithreading (the explicit goal of the 2025 Rust rewrite: "true multithreading, eliminates the GIL"), a push-based morsel-driven parallel execution engine, gRPC/HTTP server, write-ahead log, and S3-backed tiered storage. A=no prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact exists (ships native binaries, Docker, pip wheels with a compiled PyO3 .so, and an npm network client). B=N/A (not C/C++). C=impossible via mrustc~1.74: huge workspace, pervasive proc-macros (tokio, serde derive, async-trait), native threads + async network IO that do not map to wasm32-wasi single-threaded WASI; mrustc cannot build tokio-scale async/proc-macro trees. D=the Python chromadb package is a thin client over the native Rust engine (PyO3 C-extension, not pure-Python); the JS client is a network client to a server. SQLite is already live but Chroma layers HNSW native lib + tokio + threads + gRPC + object-store on top.
smoke: N/A — no buildable lane. (If forced: there is no `chroma.wasm` to fetch and `wasmtime chroma.wasm --version` cannot exist; the engine cannot start without tokio threads + a network/object-store backend.)
blocker: Native-threads-as-purpose (tokio multithreaded runtime + morsel-driven parallel engine, the explicit point of the Rust rewrite) and network/object-store-as-purpose (gRPC/HTTP server + S3 tiered storage). Even embedded mode runs only through PyO3/napi native bindings over this engine. No wasm32-wasi artifact; mrustc cannot compile a tokio/proc-macro workspace; Python client is a compiled C-extension, not pure-Python.

name: Apache Iceberg
recipe: None viable. Lane A: no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm of Iceberg or iceberg-rust exists. Lane D: no pure-Python (PyIceberg pulls pyarrow C-ext + network clients) and no JS port.

Reference impl is Java (no wasm32-wasi). PyIceberg needs pyarrow C-ext + object-store network clients. The format is designed around async object-store I/O (network-as-purpose), not local file munging. No prebuilt wasm exists.

name: Delta Lake
recipe: No viable lane. Lanes B/D inapplicable (no self-contained C/C++; Python/JS bindings just wrap the native Rust core).

Tokio multi-thread also needs native threads. No prebuilt standalone WASI .wasm exists (DuckDB delta-WASM "not yet available"). No self-contained C/C++ or pure-Python/JS port.

name: curl
recipe: N/A — no standalone wasm32-wasi lane. curl's function IS networking; wasip1 (the CommandRegistry target under wasmtime) has no raw sockets / outbound TCP. Every shipping curl-on-wasm build depends on a transport the standalone sandbox lacks: emscripten ports (libcurl.js, wapm-packages/curl) tunnel TLS over a browser WebSocket/SOCKS5 proxy (browser+JS, not wasi); Wasix builds need Wasmer/WASIX sockets (deliberately not adopted — wasmtime-only); wasip2 wasi-http / wasip3 sockets are a different component model, not the plain wasm32-wasi command lane. libcurl compiles clean under emscripten but, per upstream, has no way to open a TCP connection in the sandbox. Making curl work here would mean re-targeting it onto host-brokered Dock net imports — a bespoke host-shim build, not a prebuilt/self-contained drop-in.
smoke: N/A (impossible). Hypothetically, were a wasm32-wasi build to exist: echo run as `curl.wasm --version` then `curl.wasm -sS https://example.com` under wasmtime; it would fail at connect() — no socket in wasip1.
blocker: network-as-purpose: curl exists to move bytes over TCP/TLS, and wasm32-wasi/wasmtime (wasip1) has no raw sockets. All real curl-wasm ports rely on a browser WebSocket proxy (emscripten) or WASIX sockets (Wasmer) — neither is the standalone wasmtime sandbox. Transfers can only happen by brokering through host Dock net imports, which requires a custom host-shim port of curl, not a prebuilt or self-contained wasm artifact.

name: wget
recipe: N/A — wget's entire purpose is HTTP(S)/FTP fetch. wasm32-wasi (wasip1) has no BSD socket support, so wget cannot open network connections as a standalone .wasm under wasmtime. Networking would require host-brokered Dock net imports, which is exactly the disqualified "network-as-purpose" category. The C source is portable (Lane B buildable in principle), but build-ability is irrelevant — the runtime substrate (sockets) does not exist in the sandbox. No plain wasm32-wasi prebuilt exists (any wget.wasm is emscripten/JS-paired, not standalone wasip1).
smoke: N/A — would be `wget https://example.com/file -O out`, but no network connection is possible in-sandbox so any invocation past argument parsing fails at connect().
blocker: network-as-purpose: wget's sole function is HTTP(S)/FTP fetch; wasm32-wasi/wasip1 has no sockets, so connections are impossible without host-brokered net imports (network-as-purpose → impossible per scouting rules). Same story as curl.

name: rsync
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. rsync cannot run as standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. (1) Network-as-purpose: rsync's entire value is the SSH/socket pipe to a remote rsyncd; WASI has no sockets-as-purpose and no SSH transport. (2) fork/exec architecture: even in local mode rsync forks generator/sender/receiver processes communicating over pipes — WASI has no fork/exec. (3) select()/poll over sockets is core to the I/O loop. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi binary exists. The only "rsync wasm" artifacts (WASMrsync, fast_rsync crate, dldc-packages/librsync) are emscripten/JS-pair browser ports of the librsync *delta algorithm* for cloud delta-sync — not the rsync CLI, not wasm32-wasi, JS-coupled. The delta/rolling-checksum compute core IS pure and would compile, but stripping the network+fork-exec leaves only "improved local cp," which coreutils/cp (already LIVE) covers.
smoke: N/A — would be `rsync -a src/ dst/` for local mode, but the value prop (remote sync over SSH/socket to rsyncd) is unreachable; local-only mode is redundant with already-LIVE coreutils cp.
blocker: network-as-purpose (SSH/socket transport to remote rsyncd is the entire value) + fork/exec multi-process architecture (generator/sender/receiver) + select()/poll over sockets. WASI has none of these. Only existing wasm ports are emscripten/JS browser delta-sync of the librsync algorithm, not the wasm32-wasi rsync CLI. Local-only mode = redundant with LIVE coreutils cp.

name: gpg (GnuPG)
smoke: echo "hello" | gpg --symmetric --batch --passphrase test -o out.gpg && gpg --decrypt --batch --passphrase test out.gpg  (would need to run end-to-end under wasmtime with no host services)
blocker: GnuPG is multi-process by architecture: the gpg CLI fork/execs gpg-agent, dirmngr, gpgsm and a pinentry helper, and delegates all secret-key operations to gpg-agent over a Unix-domain socket via the Assuan IPC protocol. WASI p1 under wasmtime has no fork/exec and no Unix sockets, so the orchestrator binary (the actual deliverable) cannot function. It also needs ~/.gnupg keyring/socket dir, /dev/random and pinentry. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi gpg exists. Lane B: not a self-contained C tree — depends on libgpg-error, libgcrypt (CPU-feature asm + /dev/random), libassuan, libksba, npth (pthreads/native threads), each needing autoconf configure/codegen; and the value is the multi-process orchestration WASI forbids, not a single lib. The crypto itself is pure compute, but the proper WASI path is openpgp.js on QuickJS (Lane D) or rPGP — a DIFFERENT item, not GnuPG. Crypto primitives (libsodium, mbedtls) already live.
